title: VPC connectivity guardrails and upgrade-integration PRD for Private deployments
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: PRD describing guardrails, requirements and measurable acceptance criteria to ensure safe, auditable network connectivity and upgrade behavior for Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem) installations, minimizing blast radius for upgrades and enabling deterministic operation in air-gapped environments.
background: Customers deploying Redwood in isolated VPCs or air-gapped data centers require predictable connectivity behavior during bootstrap, scheduled upgrades, and emergency rollbacks. Past outages during staged upgrades exposed unclear operator flows around artifact fetching, operator-to-control-plane connectivity, and KMS rotations. This PRD consolidates requirements across networking, artifact delivery, upgrade orchestration, and observability so Dedicated and Private teams can implement a coordinated rollout with clear acceptance gates.
goals: Define minimal runtime networking surface required for installs and upgrades under three modes: full egress, allowlisted egress, and fully air-gapped (mirror-only)
Specify upgrade orchestration integration points (operator, sidecar, agent) and failure modes with deterministic automatic rollback triggers
Provide measurable acceptance criteria and test scenarios that QA and SRE can run in customer-simulated environments
Document operator runbooks for preflight, canary, full rollout, and rollback in isolated networks
non_goals: Designing a bespoke mirror distribution tool (we will leverage existing mirror/registry tooling)
Re-architecting the entire operator model — focus is integration and guardrails, not a rewrite
Implementing data-plane encryption protocols beyond existing KMS/HSM integrations
requirements: Network modes: system must support three explicit connectivity modes selectable at install and upgrade: 'egress-allowed', 'egress-restricted' (allowlist), 'air-gapped' (mirror-only)
Preflight checks: operator must validate all allowlist entries, DNS resolution strategy, proxy credentials, and mirror reachability before upgrade can start
Artifact integrity: every image and artifact pulled during upgrade must be validated against signed checksums; operator must refuse unsigned artifacts in air-gapped mode
KMS rotation: upgrade path must include a validated KMS key-rotation plan that can be executed offline when using an HSM proxy
Fallback channels: when primary artifact mirror is unreachable, operator must attempt two configured mirrors in order and then enter 'paused' state awaiting manual approval

Observability hooks: telemetry events emitted during preflight, staging, canary, and rollout/rollback must be queryable in Console and saved in local operator logs for 90 days (default), configurable by customer
Canary policy: support deterministic canary fraction and health probes; canary failure must trigger automatic rollback and alert generation
Timeouts and backoffs: upgrade orchestration must use exponential backoff for network retries with a configurable maximum retry window
Safe defaults: installation UX must default to 'egress-restricted' to minimize accidental exposure for new installs
Operator permissions: require least-privilege service account with documented RBAC policy for both install and upgrade operations
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: In 'egress-restricted' mode, a fresh install with only the documented allowlist (HTTP(S) endpoints and NTP) succeeds end-to-end without manual network exceptions
AC-2: Air-gapped install using a customer-provided mirror completes successfully and validates all artifacts via signature check; any unsigned artifact is rejected and surfaced in operator logs
AC-3: Running the preflight validation on a simulated degraded mirror triggers clear actionable errors and a non-destructive 'pause' state rather than partial upgrade
AC-4: Canary rollout with configured 10% fraction and synthetic liveness probe automatically rolls back when probe failure rate exceeds threshold within the canary window

AC-5: Operator emits standardized telemetry events for start, canary-start, canary-complete, rollout-start, rollout-complete, rollback, and pause; events are visible in Console runbook for the cluster
AC-6: KMS rotation during an upgrade can be executed in a zero-egress environment using an HSM proxy pattern documented in the runbook
AC-7: Customer can configure two mirror endpoints; if primary and secondary are unreachable, the operator halts upgrade and requires explicit approval to continue
AC-8: Upgrade must complete within configured SLA window when network latency to mirrors is below 200ms; if greater, operator uses a degraded path and records latency as part of the outcome
AC-9: Security review sign-off present for any change that expands default network surface; documented reviewers must sign off before merging
rollout_plan: Phase 1: implement preflight checks and network-mode flag behind feature gate; Phase 2: add artifact-signature enforcement and mirror fallback; Phase 3: integrate canary orchestration and telemetry; Phase 4: document runbooks and run customer pilots with two strategic customers. Rollout includes internal dogfood in staging and a 'mirror-only' pilot with Customer A. Each phase gated by acceptance criteria and SRE sign-off.
test_plan: Unit tests for preflight validation; integration tests that simulate allowlist-only networks using containerized firewalls; end-to-end upgrade rehearsals in QEMU-based isolated labs; chaos test injecting mirror latency and failures during canary window. QA will run the nine acceptance scenarios (AC-1..AC-9) in both AWS VPC and on-prem simulated environments.
migration_plan: For existing customers on older operator versions, provide an opt-in migration CLI that validates mirrors and generates a one-click upgrade plan. For high-risk customers, offer guided migration via Solutions Engineering. Migration must default to dry-run mode and produce an artifacts report before applying changes.

decisions: Use existing image-signing format (Cosign) for artifact validation rather than custom signing scheme
Expose network mode via install-time flag and immutable for minor upgrades to avoid unintended exposure
Provide two mirror endpoints as minimum recommended configuration for air-gapped resiliency
